gates_note: G3 traced for all three entries: every next resolves to a node or @next; no typed input (G4 pass).

best_parts: node m3_ok and m3_t24a: both PYQ key and current practice stated side by side (exam-form drill of TR24)
node m6 (appendicolith three-way probe): wrong options TR23 and TR25 each name a distinct wrong model, key is the reason-bearing one
node m5_t22: explicit 'PYQs have expected X; current practice is Y' repair for TR22
flaws: node m1: key 'Conservative: Ochsner-Sherren regimen' is the longest option of the three and the only conservative one, so the key is partly findable by form
node m3 (option 'Never needed once the lump has gone', m3_t24b) is dominated: any learner who holds the PYQ key picks the routine option over it, and no one picks it on the current-practice model
no 'Show me why' (agency) or second explanation on any trap feedback: the remediation is the same explanation re-worded, so R5 stays low
only 8 probes and no 'which is NOT' drill in exam form for the PYQ traps; TR18 tested once (m7) and TR22 tested once (m5)

best_parts: node a_why: asks for the reason behind a correct choice, so the learner must hold 'uncomplicated AND no appendicolith' rather than the headline; trap options each carry a distinct wrong model (TR22, TR23)
node g2 (Which is NOT a complication before surgery): exam-form 'NOT' stem with a correct answer that needs an operation to have happened first; directly drills TR16
nodes h1_t18a / h2_t18a feedback: name the wrong nerve, tie the incision to the nerve it splits, then re-ask in a second form (TR18 retest) before moving on
node i1 recap: one line per decision branch (operate, wait, drain) with claims, ties all three objectives
flaws: node d1_t24b ('No interval surgery or work-up is needed once it resolves') is dominated: it loses to the routine option for anyone holding the PYQ key, and no one holds the current-practice model that picks it
segment length (about 100 nodes and 12 probes for three objectives) is heavy for one segment; a tired learner gets 12 consecutive decisions before the recap
node b1: key 'Appendicectomy, because an appendicolith predicts antibiotic failure' is the only option that names the stem's finding, so it is findable by content rather than by the reasoning
node a1 and open-stem repeats: the 'Tempting:' opener repeats across most feedback nodes, which reads as a template

best_parts: node spot: classmate's three-step plan with one error to find; a clinically authentic error-spotting probe that tests whether the learner holds the mass-versus-abscess model
node interval_t24_why: both columns stated (PYQ 6-8 weeks, current selective with colonoscopy or CT in older patients) with the work-up named
node open_t22: the stem word 'only' is named as the cue to an outdated absolute, teaching the learner how to read exam keys
flaws: node comp: two-option probe with one trap (Pylephlebitis) and one key (faecal fistula) is a coin toss and diagnoses little; no 'which is NOT' form
node interval: only one trap option (TR24) so the probe does not test the 'never needed' over-correction; the trap is single-form

node spot: the key 'Step 3' is findable by content (it is the only step that introduces a change the story does not give, and the only operative step); the trap options 'Step 1' and 'Step 2' are correct statements, so a learner who knows the regimen rightly picks them and the feedback has to explain a correct step as wrong
node lith: the appendicolith is named in the stem, so the key is findable by the stem's cue; only one trap (TR23) and no second form for TR23 within this segment

merge_ideas: b's agency 'Show me why' reasoning nodes (a_why, b1_t23_why) with a's compact one-idea probes (m2, m6) and drop the 100-node length: keep one probe per trap per form
c's classmate error-spotting probe (spot) as the closing probe of the management block, with b's 'which is NOT' complication probe (g2) in place of c's two-option comp node
a's m5_t22 'PYQs have expected X; current practice is Y' repair text on every TR22/TR24 feedback, combined with b's d1_why 'older patients, over about 40' explanation
